name: Revyl

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Incomplete or non-resource economics: rates remain null, never interpreted as free.

caveats: Free 1 concurrent device per platform; Starter $250/mo includes $250 credits/3 devices, Team Pro $750 with $750/10; annual $200/$600. Overage enabled: iOS $0.15/min, Android $0.12/min. LLM uses same allowance. Enterprise dedicated iOS runners; no 4/8 sizing guaranteed.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Overage is billed only 'when enabled' (likely a toggle; default state not stated): without it, usage stops at the plan allowance. LLM (agent) usage draws down the same compute-credit allowance. Remote cloud builds also consume metered compute credits at unpublished rates.
Team Pro adds a priority device queue; Free/Starter share the standard queue (queueing, not billing). Dedicated iOS runners/instances are Enterprise/sales only.

fleet.tiers: Free 1 concurrent device per platform, Starter 3, Team Pro 10, Enterprise unlimited.
fleet.notes: Pricing variants conflict: ?plan=free describes 1 device per platform and Starter 3, while canonical page now calls entry tier Solo. Using conservative canonical one-device baseline; confirm actual subscription before large fleet.

snapshot_auto.quote: Sessions auto-terminate after 5 minutes of idle time. Call `start_device_session` to provision a new device.
snapshot_auto.note: Device sessions (iOS simulators / Android emulators) end on idle timeout or stop and the next session is a newly provisioned device; no state save/restore for users. Revyl uses snapshot-restore internally for isolation ('Simulators (iOS) and emulators (Android) give us isolation and snapshot-restore'), which is not a user feature.

own_agent_api.quote: Launch app exploration, follow each explorer, and produce an Atlas map from a terminal or CI job.
own_agent_api.note: Borderline: harness = Revyl's own device-operating AI agent, not a coding agent inside a sandbox. CLI/API/MCP start it with natural-language input (`revyl explore run --instructions ...`, `revyl device instruction "Open Settings and tap Wi-Fi"`, `revyl device validation ...`), show progress, status/cancel; Proof of Changes runs the Revyl agent per PR (`harness.kind: revyl` or `cursor`). Revyl can also launch Cursor Cloud Agent conversations and track them under Cloud Agents, but 'The agent runs in Cursor's cloud'. No Claude Code/Codex harness hosted by Revyl.

guest_firewall.quote: the platform only permits that against debuggable apps on non-rooted (Play-image) emulators
guest_firewall.note: Users get iOS simulators and non-rooted Android emulators on shared hosts, no root/shell on the host. Exception: Enterprise 'Revyl computer' dedicated Macs (revyl-computer ssh) give 'passwordless `sudo`' on an org-shared machine whose disk persists, where pf would presumably work (not documented).

secret_proxy.quote: Secret payloads can only be replaced, not viewed.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are encrypted write-only launch variables / global variables / build secret references, delivered into the app launch environment, test steps or build env. No injecting proxy.
